quality_note: Interim OpenAI production catalog. Stable role prompts define voice identity; each line defines its speech act, phrase boundary, information focus, contour, urgency, and target audible duration. Directed Hume auditions use Octave 1 because the live Octave 2 endpoint rejects utterance descriptions.

tower.instructions: American military tower controller on a busy local fighter frequency. Stable adult voice, narrow habitual pitch range, clear callsigns and numerals, natural radio compression. No announcer voice or command performance. Let the line-specific speech act determine rhythm and contour.

controller.instructions: American tactical air controller on an established fighter net. Stable adult voice, narrow habitual pitch range, clean consonants, natural radio compression. Brevity words are ordinary shared vocabulary. No announcer cadence or authority acting; use the line-specific timing and contour.

lso.instructions: American carrier landing signal officer speaking close to the microphone while watching the pass. Stable adult voice, narrow habitual pitch range, clear consonant onset. Never bark, shout, growl, add drama, or add words. Let the line-specific safety state determine timing and contour.

pilot.instructions: American single-seat fighter pilot on oxygen and a live radio net. Stable adult voice, narrow habitual pitch range, light cockpit effort in the breath, clear callsign and numerals. No cultivated coolness, heroics, or emotion acting. Let the line-specific workload and speech act determine rhythm.

traffic-two.instructions: American fighter wingman on a familiar home-station pattern frequency. Stable young-adult voice, narrow habitual pitch range, clear side number, natural radio compression. No eagerness, swagger, announcer cadence, or emotion acting.

traffic-three.instructions: American fighter wingman on a familiar home-station pattern frequency. Stable adult voice, narrow habitual pitch range, slightly rough microphone onset, clear side number. No boredom acting, swagger, or dramatic emphasis.

traffic-four.instructions: Older American fighter pilot on a familiar home-station pattern frequency. Stable mature voice, narrow habitual pitch range, slight regional vowel color, clear side number. Do not perform age, drawl, confidence, boredom, or authority.
